html:
The Battle of Omdurman was fought on 2 September 1898 outside Omdurman, near Khartoum, where a British and Egyptian army under Herbert Kitchener destroyed the army of the Mahdist state.

Kitchener had advanced up the Nile building a railway. The Khalifa's army of over 50,000 men attacked in the open and was cut down by Maxim guns, rifles and artillery. About 10,000 Sudanese were killed, against fewer than 50 on the British side. The young Winston Churchill rode in a cavalry charge that day.

Kitchener destroyed the Mahdi's tomb. The battle ended the state built after the siege of Khartoum and began the Anglo-Egyptian condominium, one of the most one-sided battles of the Scramble for Africa.
sum: The Battle of Omdurman was fought on 2 September 1898 outside Omdurman, near Khartoum, where a British and Egyptian army under Herbert Kitchener destroyed the army of the Mahdist state.
